model: Local bilinear response with physical output decoding; midpoint mask refresh (10 steps) versus original unrefreshed evolution
arms: signed response-matched copies (2,-1), metrics output .5 / incoming .2
primary_targets: Peer minus no-pressure common-output correction gain
Signed minus peer common-output correction gain
primary_score: RMSE of contrast predictions, pooled seeds,widths,horizons; resample whole seeds for uncertainty
quantitative_hypothesis: Refreshed-model contrast RMSE below .5 times zero-effect RMSE, and below original model RMSE
causal_hypothesis: Signed copies reduce response drift; they improve first-step correction in states forecast to suffer peer-induced first-step impairment, while also suppressing beneficial changes
width_hypothesis: Negative part of relative peer-induced first-step gain change is smaller on average at width128; no monotone long-term benefit presumed
limitation: Pilot shows short-lived impairments and gain-order reversals. Lower V_tau alone is not a finite-horizon failure predictor; no uniform 20-step or native-recovery rescue predicted.
diagnostic: Frozen-quadratic finite-budget response uses the same Jacobian/curvature and is compared with realized correction; no new fitted parameters
cohort: Ten fresh initialization seeds, one assigned focal class per seed covering digits0-9. Class and initialization effects are not independently replicated.
chronology: After selected-case pilot and signed-copy pilot; quadratic diagnostic pilot running; no fresh intervention results available.
